items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline names the pick (Atlas-M) and the risk (resolve rate exactly on its 90% line). The decision block gives why each other model is out: Atlas-L over p95 in four of five tasks, Brisk-S under the quality floor in four, Open-70B at 89% against 95% on speculation. c1 and its gate matrix show Atlas-M as the only column with no Fails cell. A reader can act from this screen alone and knows which result to watch.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 says Atlas-M is the only option that passes. c2 and c3 show its two thin gates: resolves at 90% on the line, and research p95 at 2.84 s against 3 s. c4 shows its cost, 2 to 5 points of overall quality below Atlas-L. Nothing contradicts the headline. The explore rows match decision_sensitivity: no model passes below 2.84 s, Atlas-L becomes eligible from 4.86 s, and any resolve line above 90% leaves the troubleshooting task with no passing model.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's weak axes are all shown: it sits on the resolve line, its research p95 margin has no interval, and it is lower on quality. The fallback is overstated, though. The lede calls Atlas-L 'the only other model that resolves troubleshooting issues at or above the line' and frames the fallback as 'a trade between resolving issues and speed'. Atlas-L leads Atlas-M on resolves by only 1 point, with an interval of -5.1 to +7.1 (arms_compare). Atlas-L's own interval, 86.8% to 95.2%, also straddles the line. The 'watch' slot says a re-run is 'as likely to land below it as above', but the best_of_n caveat says a fresh run tends to read lower. c4 says Atlas-M is lower 'in every task but speculation bait', yet it is lower there too (-1); that gap is just within noise.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: I checked each omission against the snapshot. Atlas-M's other gate gaps are all at least 3 points or 0.16 s, and its quality half-widths are 1.1 to 1.8, so none is borderline. The cheaper single-task routes and Open-70B's borderline billing quality are moot because both models fail speculation, which applies to all traffic. count.examples = 0, so the 'no failure examples' omission is true. One gap: the 'no model passes' fallback hides that only troubleshooting (19% of traffic) would lose its passing model. Atlas-M still passes billing, persona and research when the resolve line rises (decision_sensitivity on threshold:trouble.resolves). This does not change today's call.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All four snapshot caveats (best_of_n, judge_unstated, point_estimate:p95, no_control) are shown. Each has a specific material_if that says what would move the call, and each except no_control has a matching next step: a fresh larger set, judge calibration, and a p95 interval. no_control is scoped correctly to the quality comparison, not to the gate-based call.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: All five next steps name an experiment or a declaration and what it would settle. These are: improve and re-run troubleshooting, a larger fresh set, naming and calibrating the resolve judge, a p95 interval, and declaring volume and a price per point. The second step gives no case count. settle_cases refuses to size it because the estimate sits exactly on the line, so that omission is defensible. The parenthetical '(clear steps, escalation)' in the first step suggests a cause the data does not show: Atlas-M clears both gates by 5 points.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Each block is the right form for its claim. c1 uses a gate matrix for a pass/fail-by-task claim. c2 uses a dot-interval with the floor for an on-the-line claim, and its interval of 85.6% to 94.4% is the interval cited. c3 uses range bars with the budget, and 2.84 s is the nearest Atlas-M bar end. c4 uses diverging bars with unpaired intervals for the quality gap, where troubleshooting at -5 is the largest. Each counterfactual holds: for example, if Atlas-M's troubleshooting dot sat at 93%, c2 and the headline's risk would change.

findings.finding: The lede and the next/watch slots frame the fallback as 'a trade between resolving issues and speed', with Atlas-L as the model that resolves at or above the line. Atlas-L leads Atlas-M on troubleshooting resolves by +1 point (interval -5.1 to +7.1), and its own interval of 86.8% to 95.2% also straddles 90%. If Atlas-M's true rate is under the line, Atlas-L's may be too, so the fallback is not clearly a resolve-for-latency trade. Say that Atlas-L is level with Atlas-M on resolving, and that only its higher quality and slower p95 separate them.

'No model passes' in the lede, the caveats and the explore rows hides the scope of the failure. Above a 90% resolve line, only troubleshooting (19% of traffic) loses its passing model, and Atlas-M still passes billing, persona and research (decision_sensitivity on threshold:trouble.resolves). The contingency a reader needs is about the troubleshooting task, not a whole-traffic re-choice.

The watch slot says a re-run 'is as likely to land below it as above'. The best_of_n caveat says a fresh run 'tends to read it lower'. Reconcile them: as the pick of four, a re-run is more likely to land below than above.

The c4 text says Atlas-M scores lower 'in every task but speculation bait'. It is lower there too (-1). The interval of -3.546 to +1.546 spans zero, so the gap is within noise. Write 'clearly lower in every task but speculation bait, where the gap is within noise'.

The explore price row prints the center as {price...per_point|usd_per_1k} ($14.76 per 1,000 conversations) and the ends as |usd ($11.09, $22.05), with no unit. Use |usd_per_1k on the low and high keys too; it reads as '$11.09 per 1,000 conversations'.

The first next step's '(clear steps, escalation)' suggests a cause the data does not support: Atlas-M clears both of those gates by 5 points. Either drop the parenthetical or ground it in failure examples, of which none were kept.

invariant_concerns: None blocking. All 34 cited figure keys read on the snapshot (figure_keys_check, none unstated or refused). All four snapshot caveats are shown with material_if, and the confidence form high_if_immaterial matches open caveats. Method is present. Above the appendix, the only ids are caveat ids in their structural field.

Rendering note, not the report's text: in the gate matrix, Atlas-L persona prints '$41.0' and Atlas-M speculation prints '$19.0', while other cells drop the trailing .0. The cost precision is inconsistent within one block.
